title: Dispatch fresh authenticated Hostinger build evidence after secret configuration

phases.objective: Provide a fresh single-use authorization bridge with an explicit expected-main-SHA dispatch input that starts the existing trusted-main GET-only Hostinger Node.js build-history workflow after the repository secret is configured.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: An explicit repository-owner workflow dispatch or an exact governed issue comment supplies the current trusted main SHA while Incident #4953 remains open.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Before the first metadata write, the bridge resolves and validates an explicit expected main SHA, verifies the immutable authorization comment, workflow blob, current main head, protected Production SHA, and one-time marker absence; then it dispatches the unchanged GET-only evidence workflow and records its run ID without performing any provider mutation.
steps: Resolve the explicit expected main SHA from the required workflow_dispatch input or the exact governed issue-comment token.
Validate the operator identity, issue number when applicable, and exact 40-character expected main SHA before any write.
Validate the fresh authorization comment and its workflow blob, account, domain, Production SHA, merge timestamp, and GET-only boundaries.
Reject execution if main, Production, the workflow blob, or incident state changed.
Record a one-time claim in Issue #4953.
Dispatch the unchanged trusted-main Hostinger evidence workflow with bounded inputs.
Resolve the newly created workflow run and record its run ID for evidence collection.
assertions: Every write-capable execution path requires an explicit expected main SHA and checks it against current main before the first metadata write.
The issue-comment trigger remains exact-token, exact-operator, and exact-issue bounded, while workflow_dispatch is repository-owner bounded.
The bridge never receives or references the Hostinger secret value.
The target workflow alone reads secrets.HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN on trusted main.
The Hostinger provider operation is GET-only and performs no build creation, deployment, restart, or provider mutation.
No repository contents mutation, protected-ref update, force push, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, or external send is introduced.
The authorization binding cannot be reused after a claim or dispatch marker exists.

phases.objective: Observe one fresh authenticated Hostinger build-history artifact and record its bounded classification in Incident #4953.
Confirm the bridge fails closed when the explicit head input, main, Production, authorization, workflow blob, incident state, or one-time markers diverge.
This workflow reads build history only and performs no Hostinger canary or provider mutation.
This workflow does not deploy, restart, or mutate Production.
